current_example.problem:
What is the solution to the following system of inequalities?

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2-7x\ge 2 \\ 10x-3\ge 7\end{aligned}
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
To solve the system, we need to find the values of $x$ that satisfy both $2-7x \geq 2$ and $10x-3 \geq 7$ simultaneously. 

- First, we solve $2-7x \geq 2\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}2-7x & \ge 2 \\ 2-7x-2 & \ge 2-2 \\ -7x & \ge 0 \\ (-1)\cdot (-7x) & \le (-1)\cdot 0 \\ 7x & \le 0 \\ \frac{7x}{7} & \le \frac{0}{7} \\ x & \le 0\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/96957d6e6c105fd3734dbe478850287c1c8771873b94fedc4ee0ed5cebf41c40.png)

- Then, we solve $10x-3 \geq 7\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}10x-3 & \ge 7 \\ 10x-3+3 & \ge 7+3 \\ 10x & \ge 10 \\ \frac{10x}{10} & \ge \frac{10}{10} \\ x & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/9d2d2e7b05bd4bcaf964353266e35bb12f406372ade7255accf6dc3503046f5c.png)

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/98654d9ff727e680d0e1ba1ff88b9202248aba6a75a5002a01cd9d628cb6c5b3.png)

It turns out that the solutions do not overlap at all. Therefore, no values of $x$ satisfy both inequalities simultaneously. So, there is no solution.
